source.title: Generalizing and Decoupling Neural Collapse via Hyperspherical Uniformity Gap
source.authors: Wei-Yang Liu; Long-Hui Yu; Adrian Weller; B. Schölkopf

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices supplied
record.tranche_reason: Reports test error for HUG and cross-entropy across datasets, architectures, and learning scenarios, and measures feature geometry during training. These are conceptual tests of generalization and properties proposed to track it, but do not test the listed original interventions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error comparisons for HUG versus cross-entropy, training dynamics of hyperspherical energy and reverse-energy, and loss-landscape visualizations. Cited results about arbitrary-label fitting and other prior work are not rows. Figure-only training-dynamics values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests HUG versus cross-entropy and generalized neural collapse, neither of which is a listed claim version. It cites arbitrary-label fitting and invokes a flatness–generalization heuristic, but does not test random-label generalization, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus full connectivity, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps, or memorized-example removal.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors propose generalized neural collapse and a HUG framework that decouples inter-class separability from intra-class variability. They report HUG variants outperforming CE in tested classification and adversarial-robustness settings, while acknowledging greater hyperparameter sensitivity, possible convergence instability, and the need for larger-scale validation. These conclusions do not establish any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and evaluates a new hyperspherical-uniformity-gap loss against cross-entropy; it does not reproduce the listed random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-gap, or memorized-example interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture (ResNet-18, VGG-16, DenseNet-121); dataset (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-2012, and stated NLP tasks); loss variant (MHE-HUG, MHS-HUG, MGD-HUG); proxy update method; imbalance ratio; memory size; attack strength; feature dimension and class count. The paper also notes HUG losses are more sensitive to hyperparameters and may be less stable to train than CE.

fits_no_version.finding: HUG variants and proxy-update choices reduce reported CIFAR test error relative to CE; MHE-HUG gives 5.03% versus 5.45% on CIFAR-10 and 23.50% versus 24.90% on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HUG can improve held-out classification performance over CE in the tested architectures and recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: HUG improves reported long-tailed, continual-learning, perturbed-test, and NLP outcomes relative to CE. The record reverses dataset assignments in Tables 4–5, and Table 6 has inconsistent clean-metric labeling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HUG can outperform CE across the tested learning scenarios, subject to correcting dataset assignments and resolving the clean-metric inconsistency.

fits_no_version.finding: HUG's loss landscape is described as flatter than CE's, but the study does not establish magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The plotted HUG objective has qualitatively flatter local landscapes than CE under the paper's visualization procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-mean and classifier energy decrease during training, and within-class feature variability declines, supporting the paper's generalized neural-collapse hypothesis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained feature and classifier geometry approaches hyperspherical uniformity and within-class collapse in the tested settings.

record.problems: The paper reports test metrics but no uncertainty estimates in the supplied tables. Feature-geometry curves are figures without extracted numeric values. The qualitative loss-landscape comparison is presented as potentially indicating stronger generalization, but the study does not directly report a train-test gap or test whether the measured properties track that gap. Authors themselves state more large-scale experiments are needed and mention hyperparameter sensitivity and possible instability.
record.rows_left_out: none; 40 rows retained, including grouped table values where the source reports them together.

untested.parts: Own experiments comparing random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe; arbitrary-label fitting is cited only.
Width beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and changes to training duration or recipe.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Influence-defined memorization and retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states remain cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not mean the reported HUG improvements are absent. The study is not T2 merely because it reports held-out performance. Its loss comparisons and geometry measurements address different questions. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a version-specific verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparison and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch-size generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps among networks with similarly low training loss.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
